The Harness Is the Machine: How to Build Unbreakable AI Agents with Claude Code & Claude 5.5 
A complete architectural guide to task contracts, isolated worktrees, adversarial verification, and the compounding flywheel across Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, and Fable 5.5
bookmark this and read the complete production agent playbook below ↓
THE 30-SECOND ANSWER
When an autonomous AI agent fails 14 turns into a multi-file refactor, most developers make the same mistake
They rewrite the prompt
Then they switch models
Then they upgrade to a larger context window
The agent still forgets earlier decisions. It still modifies the wrong files. It still outputs: All 48 unit tests passed successfully, without running a test runner
The failure comes from the environment around the model. That environment is the harness. Designing it is Harness Engineering
Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, explained this during the launch of Claude Code:
Of course, you need an interface, you need a harness to use them
The model is the engine. The harness is the machine
Put Claude Sonnet 5.5 into an unmanaged chat window, and it achieves an 18% success rate on complex multi-file engineering tasks. Put that same model into an engineered harness with path boundaries, isolated git worktrees, sub-second linter sensors, and adversarial verification, and task completion reaches 95%
Below is the complete architectural blueprint for building production autonomous agents using Claude Code and the Anthropic 5.5 model stack across Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Haiku 5.5, and Fable 5.5
System Architecture Pipeline
Stage 1: Pre-Flight Task Contract
Human intent compiles into a bounded task_contract.json via Claude Opus 5.5
Stage 2: Sandboxed Worktree Isolation
Harness spawns an isolated git worktree before any tool executes
Stage 3: Autonomous Implementation
Claude Sonnet 5.5 executes code modifications within strict path allowlists
Stage 4: Sub-Second Sensor Interception
Claude Haiku 5.5 validates every bash tool call and parameter in real time
Stage 5: Adversarial Red-Teaming
Claude Fable 5.5 attacks the diff, searching race conditions and edge cases
Stage 6: Deterministic Evidence Gate
Physical pre-commit hook verifies test output and signs receipt.json
Stage 7: Compounding Memory Flywheel
Failures crystallize into permanent rules, skills, and regression evals on disk
1. The Anatomy of Failure: Chat Window vs. Production Harness
Observing the same model across two operating environments explains why autonomous agents break down:
System Breakdown: Raw Chat Window vs. Engineered Harness
Execution Surface
Raw Chat: Flat string buffer with interleaved chat history
Engineered Harness: Sandboxed git worktree filesystem plus state ledger files
Task Boundaries
Raw Chat: Open-ended conversational prompt (e.g. Refactor auth)
Engineered Harness: Machine-readable JSON contract with strict path allowlists
Tool Execution
Raw Chat: Unchecked tool calls where the model self-approves syntax
Engineered Harness: Pre-tool hooks and static typecheckers intercepting all inputs
State Persistence
Raw Chat: Transient context window that dies when the session terminates
Engineered Harness: Durable append-only ledger persisted directly to disk
Verification Logic
Raw Chat: Model validates itself and claims the code works
Engineered Harness: Decoupled skeptic agent (Claude Fable 5.5) proving test logs
Failure Recovery
Raw Chat: Human reprompts while the model invents new excuses
Engineered Harness: Automatic rollback to clean checkpoint hash, recording failure to evals
End-to-End Success Rate
Raw Chat: 18% completion on complex multi-turn workflows
Engineered Harness: 95% deterministic task convergence
When an agent runs in a chat window, context pollution compounds with every turn. By turn 8, earlier instructions drown under thousands of tokens of raw tool output. The model begins guessing parameter names and enters repetitive error loops
The harness converts conversation into stateful software infrastructure
2. The Anthropic 5.5 Model Matrix inside Claude Code
Building production agents on a single model fails economically. Running Opus 5.5 for file linting burns budget at $15 per million tokens. Running Haiku 5.5 for system decomposition breaks the architecture
A production harness uses role specialization:
The Claude 5.5 Harness Role Division
Claude Opus 5.5 (Lead Architect and Arbiter)
Assignment: Generates task contracts, reviews architectural invariants, settles merge conflicts
Economics: High reasoning depth at $15.00 per million tokens
Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Autonomous Engineer)
Assignment: Writes production code, modifies modules, executes bash tool calls
Economics: Fast agentic coding at $3.00 per million tokens
Claude Haiku 5.5 (Sub-Second Gatekeeper)
Assignment: Validates tool parameters, enforces path bounds, runs linters
Economics: Millisecond response latency at $0.25 per million tokens
Claude Fable 5.5 (Adversarial Skeptic)
Assignment: Attacks code diffs, fuzzes boundary cases, searches race conditions
Economics: Hostile security red-teaming at $2.50 per million tokens
3. Principle 1: The Pre-Flight Task Contract (Zero Token 1 Generation)
An autonomous agent must not write code from conversational instructions. Before Claude Sonnet 5.5 generates token 1, Claude Opus 5.5 compiles a machine-readable task_contract.json
The contract defines four boundaries:
1. Path Boundary (filesystem_boundary): Explicit list of files the agent can read and edit. Any attempt to touch .env or root package files triggers an immediate interrupt
2. Economic Envelope (budget): Hard limits on dollar spend, conversation turns, and wall-clock execution seconds
3. Acceptance Invariants (acceptance_criteria): Deterministic shell commands that must exit with code 0
4. Required Artifacts (required_evidence): Verification files that must exist on disk before the task closes

**한 줄 평: 방향은 맞지만, 숫자와 코드는 믿으면 안 되는 글이에요.** 아이디어는 쓸 만해요. 근거와 구현 예시는 상당 부분 틀렸거나 확인할 수 없어요.

## 1. 핵심 주장
- 에이전트가 실패하는 원인은 모델보다 모델을 둘러싼 환경(harness)에 있다.
- 그래서 7단계 파이프라인을 제안해요: 계약 → worktree 격리 → 구현 → 도구 호출 검사 → 적대적 검증 → 증거 게이트 → 실패를 규칙으로 축적.

이 주장 자체는 업계에서 널리 받아들여지는 생각이에요.

## 2. 사실 오류와 근거가 없는 부분

| 항목 | 문제 |
|---|---|
| 성공률 18% → 95% | 출처도 측정 방법도 없어요. |
| Dario Amodei 인용 | 출처가 없어요. 확인할 수 없어요. |
| "Fable 5.5" | 제가 아는 최신 Fable은 5.2예요. 5.5는 없는 모델일 가능성이 커요. |
| 가격 ($15 / $3 / $0.25 / $2.50) | 옛 세대 가격표와 비슷해 보여요. 현재 가격은 따로 확인해야 해요. |
| `anthropic.com/schemas/agent-contract-v1.json` | 제가 아는 한 Anthropic 공식 표준이 아니에요. |
| `claude --dangerously-skip-permissions false` | 값을 받지 않는 플래그예요. 이렇게 써도 의도대로 동작하지 않아요. |

## 3. 코드가 실제로는 동작하지 않아요
**pre-tool.sh (가장 큰 문제)**
- Claude Code hook은 입력을 stdin의 JSON으로 받아요. `$1`, `$2` 위치 인자로 받지 않아요.
- 도구 호출을 막으려면 exit code 2를 써야 해요. `exit 1`은 막지 않고 그냥 지나가요.
- 결과적으로 이 "보안 게이트"는 아무것도 막지 못해요.
- 영수증도 `head -n 1`로 아무 파일이나 하나 집어요. 현재 작업의 영수증인지 확인하지 않아요.

**receipt.json**
- `cryptographic_signature`는 16자리 문자열일 뿐이에요. 서명이 아니에요.
- 영수증을 에이전트가 직접 쓰니 에이전트가 위조할 수 있어요. 이러면 게이트 의미가 없어요.

**audit-diff.sh**
- `src/auth/` 같은 디렉터리 항목은 `[[ == ]]` 비교에서 매칭되지 않아요.
- 따옴표 없이 단어를 나눠서 공백이 들어간 경로에서 깨져요.

**"Haiku가 모든 bash 호출을 1초 안에 검사"**
- 매 호출마다 LLM을 부르면 지연과 비용이 쌓여요.
- 경로 검사 같은 일은 LLM보다 결정적인 스크립트가 더 빠르고 정확해요.

## 4. 그래도 쓸 만한 아이디어
- 생성과 검증 분리: 자기 코드를 자기가 검증하게 하지 않기.
- 완료 조건을 "exit 0이 나와야 하는 명령"으로 정의하기.
- 작업마다 worktree로 격리하기. Claude Code에 이미 기능이 있어요.
- 실패를 규칙, 테스트, 메모리로 남겨 다음 세션에 재사용하기.
- 비용과 턴 수에 상한 두기.

# Verification Evidence — decisions, done criteria, limits of a check

Rules for how a skill reports finished work, so the user can stand behind it. Most agent output is well written and mostly right. That makes it easy to accept without a second look. These rules put three things in front of the user that a summary hides: what the agent decided on its own, what was actually run to prove the result, and what that proof does not cover.

Scope: a skill applies this file when its MD links here (today `create-program` Phase 8 and `analyze-symptom`). Rule 2's fixed-up-front Done Criteria apply to skills that build something (`create-program`); an analysis skill (`analyze-symptom`) has no pass target, so its Evidence lines say `supports` / `contradicts` / `not run` relative to the stated root cause instead of PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN. It changes the report only — no extra MCP calls, no extra agents, same cost in `standard` and `eco`.

## Rule 1 — Decisions & Assumptions section

Every final deliverable carries a section **Decisions & Assumptions** listing the choices the agent made that the user did not state explicitly. One line each:

`- <decision> — why: <reason> · to change: <what the user would do>`

What belongs here:

| Kind | Example |
|---|---|
| Default chosen | ALV layout save allowed for all users; date range defaults to current month |
| Out of scope | No authorization check on plant (not in the spec); no batch variant |
| Conflict resolved | Spec said "show all items", interview said "open items only" → open items only |
| Unverified assumption | Assumed `ZMMT0012-STATUS` values are `A`/`I` only (domain has no fixed values) |
| Scope narrowing | Read the failing include only, not the whole program; transports of the last 7 days only |

What does not belong: choices the user made in the interview (a default the agent proposed and the user only acknowledged with ok / yes does belong — the user did not choose it), choices fixed by a `common/` rule (naming, field typing), and restating the spec. If there is nothing to list, write the heading with "None — every choice came from the spec or the user." Never drop the section.

Order: most consequential first. Cap at 10 lines; past 10, group the rest by kind ("+ 6 text-element defaults").

## Rule 2 — Done criteria fixed up front, evidence shown first

A skill states what "verified" means **before** the work starts, as a short list of factual checks — a tool call and the result that counts as pass. Example for a program:

| Check | Pass |
|---|---|
| `ActivateObjects` on every created object | no error messages |
| `GetInactiveObjects` | none of this run's objects listed |
| `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis(<main program>)` — includes are not checked standalone | no errors |
| `RunUnitTest` (when Phase 5 ran) | all tests green, count > 0 |

Do not redefine "done" after the result is in. If a check could not run (tool missing, ECC limit, user skipped Phase 5), the result is **not run** — never pass.

In the report, the **Evidence** block comes before the summary. One line per check:

`- <tool> <target> → <result as returned, short excerpt> — PASS | FAIL | NOT RUN`

Quote the returned value (message text, count, object list); do not paraphrase it into "looks fine". The summary may only claim what an evidence line shows.

## Rule 3 — What the check does not prove

Each PASS line, or the Evidence block as a whole, carries the limits of that check:

`  ↳ does not prove: <property the check cannot see>`

Typical limits:

| Check | Does not prove |
|---|---|
| Activation / syntax check | business logic is right; runtime behavior with real data |
| `GetInactiveObjects` empty | objects are on the right transport |
| Unit tests green | cases the tests do not cover; tests written with the same mistake as the code pass too |
| Code review PASS | only the conventions reviewed; not the requirement itself |
| Dump explained by the source | that this is the only path to the dump; that the fix has no side effects |
| A tool's success message | that the target screen (SE80, Form Painter, SM30) shows it the same way |

End the report with one line that names the one thing a person should still check by hand before relying on the result (for example "Run the program once in DEV with a real plant and compare the totals with MB52").

## Placement in a report

```
## Evidence            ← Rule 2 (+ Rule 3 lines)
## Summary             ← claims backed by Evidence only
## Decisions & Assumptions   ← Rule 1
## Still check by hand ← Rule 3 closing line
```

A skill whose output format already has its own sections keeps them and inserts these where its MD says.

## Language

Localize the section headings to the report language. The verdict tokens (PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN, supports / contradicts / not run) stay in English.

| Dump explained by the source | that this is the only path to the dump; that the fix has no side effects |
| A tool's success message | that the target screen (SE80, Form Painter, SM30) shows it the same way |

End the report with one line that names the one thing a person should still check by hand before relying on the result (for example "Run the program once in DEV with a real plant and compare the totals with MB52").

## Placement in a report

```
## Evidence            ← Rule 2 (+ Rule 3 lines)
## Summary             ← claims backed by Evidence only
## Decisions & Assumptions   ← Rule 1
## Still check by hand ← Rule 3 closing line
```

A skill whose output format already has its own sections keeps them and inserts these where its MD says.

## Language

Localize the section headings to the report language. The verdict tokens (PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN, supports / contradicts / not run) stay in English.

**네, 스크립트로 할 수 있어요.** 에이전트가 쓰지 않고 MCP 응답 원문을 hook이 기록하는 구조로 만들면 돼요. 코드를 확인해 보니 바탕이 되는 규칙은 이미 있어요.

## 확인한 현황
- `common/verification-evidence.md` Rule 2에 완료 조건이 이미 정해져 있어요. 활성화, 비활성 객체 0개, unit test 통과예요.
- 그런데 Evidence 블록은 지금 에이전트가 직접 써요. 그래서 위조나 착각을 막을 장치가 없어요.
- `hooks/hooks.json`에는 `PostToolUse` hook이 없어요. `PostToolUseFailure`만 있어요.
- MCP 응답은 JSON이라 스크립트로 읽을 수 있어요.
  - `ActivateObjects`는 `success`, `failed_count`, `errors`, `objects`를 돌려줘요.
  - `RunUnitTest`는 ECC에서 결과를 바로 `run_result`로 줘요. 그 밖의 시스템에서는 `GetUnitTestResult`로 따로 받아요.
- **주의할 점:** `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis`는 SAP 문법 검사가 아니에요. 넘겨받은 소스를 로컬에서 분석할 뿐이에요. 그래서 문법 검사 증거는 `ActivateObjects` 결과(preaudit 포함)로 삼아야 해요.

## 설계안

**1. 기록기: PostToolUse hook (`scripts/evidence/record.mjs`)**
- 대상 도구는 `ActivateObjects`, `GetInactiveObjects`, `RunUnitTest`, `GetUnitTestResult`예요.
- MCP 응답을 그대로 `.sc4sap/evidence/{session}.jsonl`에 한 줄씩 덧붙여요. 시각, 도구, 입력, 응답 해시를 함께 남겨요.
- 서브에이전트가 부른 호출도 hook이 잡아요.

**2. 영수증 생성: `scripts/evidence/build-receipt.mjs {PROG}`**
- 기록에서 `{PROG}` 관련 객체만 골라 Rule 2 기준으로 판정해요.
- 판정 결과를 `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/receipt.json`에 써요. 항목마다 PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN이에요.
- 테스트가 0건이면 NOT RUN이에요. PASS로 치지 않아요.
- 활성화 이후에 소스를 다시 고쳤다면 그 활성화 결과는 무효로 처리해요.

**3. 게이트: create-program Phase 8**
- 보고서의 Evidence 블록을 `receipt.json`에서 생성해요. 에이전트는 더 이상 Evidence를 직접 쓰지 않아요.
- 영수증이 없거나 FAIL이 있으면 "완료"라고 보고할 수 없어요.

**4. 위조 방지**
- 기존 PreToolUse hook을 넓혀서 `.sc4sap/evidence/`와 `receipt.json`에 Write, Edit, Bash 쓰기를 막아요.

## 이 영수증이 증명하지 못하는 것
- 비즈니스 로직이 맞는지는 증명하지 못해요.
- 테스트가 다루지 않는 경우도 보장하지 못해요.
- SAP TCode에서 사용자가 직접 확인하는 단계는 그대로 남아요.

## 작업 범위 (sc4sap 저장소만)
- 스크립트 2개와 `hooks.json`
- `phase8` / `verification-evidence.md` 수정 (200줄 제한 지켜서)
- 단위 테스트 (실제 MCP 응답 샘플 사용)

## Phase 7 — Debug escalation: `sap-debugger` (dispatch with `model: "opus"`)
- Activation failures persisting after retry
- Runtime dumps during test execution

## Phase 8 — Completion Report: `sap-writer` (Sonnet override)

> **Model**: dispatch `sap-writer` with **`model: "sonnet"` override** — base Haiku is sufficient for pure templating, but the Phase 8 report aggregates review verdicts + timing metrics + transport metadata + convention-compliance narrative, which `common/model-routing-rule.md` Per-wave table classifies as Sonnet tier. The report is the skill's final deliverable to the user; light reasoning over structured state keeps wording precise without paying Opus cost.
>
> ```
> ▶ phase=8 (writer-report) · agent=sap-writer · model=Sonnet
> ```

Dispatch input (writer receives, does NOT re-fetch via MCP):

- **Pre-condition (HARD GATE, enforced by main before dispatching)**: `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/review.md` must exist and end in PASS verdicts for every applicable convention. If missing or contains unresolved violations, return to Phase 6 — do not dispatch Phase 8 and do not tell the user the program is done.
- Objects created + activation status
- Transport number
- Test results summary (Phase 5, if run)
- Reference to `review.md` (Phase 6 verdicts)
- **Timing summary** — per-phase `timing` / `sec` fields from `state.json` so the writer can render the total-duration table (Phase 4 parallel gains, Phase 6 bucket gains, Opus escalation ratio)
- User conversation language (so the report localizes — Korean / English / Japanese / etc.)
- spec.md § *9. Done Criteria* and the files holding their results — the writer reads these, it does not re-fetch: `verify-phase4.md` (semantic-analysis / activation lines + inactive-list CHECKER blocks, newest wins), Phase 5 `GetUnitTestResult` output, `review.md` § 12 Activation State; plus `decisions.md` and plan.md § *Conflict Resolutions*

**Report rules** — [`../../common/verification-evidence.md`](../../common/verification-evidence.md): Evidence block first (one line per Done Criteria check, PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN with the returned value, plus its "does not prove" line), then the summary, then *Decisions & Assumptions* (from `decisions.md` + conflict resolutions + interview defaults the agent proposed and the user only acknowledged with ok / yes), then one *Still check by hand* line. A check with no result in those files is NOT RUN. A FAIL or NOT RUN is reported as such — never folded into "done".

Output:
- File: `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/report.md` (written by the writer agent)
- In `manual`/`hybrid` mode: main prompts the user before dispatching Phase 8
- **HTML copies (optional, after the report is shown)**: close with one line — *"Also want HTML copies of spec.md and report.md? (y/N)"* (a closing question, not a phase-transition prompt, so it applies in `auto` mode too). On yes, run `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/spec/md-to-html.mjs" <file>.md` for each (`<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = two levels above this skill folder) → single-file `.html` beside it. The `.md` files stay — they are pipeline state (resume, review).

## State.json — Resume Support (C-2)

All phases above record their completion into `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/state.json` per the schema in [`execution-mode.md`](./execution-mode.md). On a subsequent invocation for the same `{PROG}`, the skill:
1. Reads `state.json` and finds the first non-completed, non-skipped phase
2. Resumes from that phase, skipping all preceding ones
3. In `auto` mode, resumption happens silently; in `manual`/`hybrid`, the user is shown the resume point and asked to confirm

- User conversation language (so the report localizes — Korean / English / Japanese / etc.)
- spec.md § *9. Done Criteria* and the files holding their results — the writer reads these, it does not re-fetch: `verify-phase4.md` (semantic-analysis / activation lines + inactive-list CHECKER blocks, newest wins), Phase 5 `GetUnitTestResult` output, `review.md` § 12 Activation State; plus `decisions.md` and plan.md § *Conflict Resolutions*

**Report rules** — [`../../common/verification-evidence.md`](../../common/verification-evidence.md): Evidence block first (one line per Done Criteria check, PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN with the returned value, plus its "does not prove" line), then the summary, then *Decisions & Assumptions* (from `decisions.md` + conflict resolutions + interview defaults the agent proposed and the user only acknowledged with ok / yes), then one *Still check by hand* line. A check with no result in those files is NOT RUN. A FAIL or NOT RUN is reported as such — never folded into "done".

Output:
- File: `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/report.md` (written by the writer agent)
- In `manual`/`hybrid` mode: main prompts the user before dispatching Phase 8
- **HTML copies (optional, after the report is shown)**: close with one line — *"Also want HTML copies of spec.md and report.md? (y/N)"* (a closing question, not a phase-transition prompt, so it applies in `auto` mode too). On yes, run `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/spec/md-to-html.mjs" <file>.md` for each (`<PLUGIN_ROOT>` = two levels above this skill folder) → single-file `.html` beside it. The `.md` files stay — they are pipeline state (resume, review).

## State.json — Resume Support (C-2)

All phases above record their completion into `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/state.json` per the schema in [`execution-mode.md`](./execution-mode.md). On a subsequent invocation for the same `{PROG}`, the skill:
1. Reads `state.json` and finds the first non-completed, non-skipped phase
2. Resumes from that phase, skipping all preceding ones
3. In `auto` mode, resumption happens silently; in `manual`/`hybrid`, the user is shown the resume point and asked to confirm

This file is the **index** of development rules — NOT a payload to preload. Detailed rules live in `common/` and `exceptions/`. Consult files on demand per [`common/context-loading-protocol.md`](common/context-loading-protocol.md) — 4-tier model: **Tier 1** global mandatory safety baseline (always loaded by every agent: `data-extraction-policy`, `sap-version-reference`, `naming-conventions`; `context-loading-protocol` + `model-routing-rule` are orchestrator-only, read by skills), **Tier 2** role-mandatory per agent group, **Tier 3** triggered reads, **Tier 4** per-task kit. Everything referenced below is MANDATORY for every sc4sap session (agents, skills, direct user requests, pipelines).

Before any work: verify `.sc4sap/config.json` exists and contains `sapVersion`, `abapRelease`, `industry`. Every recommendation, piece of generated code, and tool invocation must respect those fields.

## Critical Rules (summary — full text in referenced files)

1. **Custom objects use `Z`/`Y` prefix.** Full rules: `common/naming-conventions.md`.
2. **Match SAP version and ABAP release.** Never use S/4-only tables on ECC or syntax newer than the configured `abapRelease`. Full rules: `common/sap-version-reference.md`, `common/abap-release-reference.md`.
3. **Transport discipline.** Every change goes on a transport. Description format: `[MODULE] [Action] [Object] - [brief]`. Never release with syntax errors or inactive objects. Every `CreateTransport` call must receive an explicit `client` parameter resolved from `.sc4sap/sap.env` SAP_CLIENT (full rule: `common/transport-client-rule.md`).
4. **Activate after every change.** Run `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` for syntax, then `GetInactiveObjects` to confirm no leftovers. Follow Clean ABAP conventions: `common/clean-code.md` (shared) + the paradigm-specific companion (`clean-code-oop.md` OR `clean-code-procedural.md`).
5. **Data extraction is gated.** Before any `GetTableContents` / `GetSqlQuery`: consult `exceptions/table_exception.md` and `common/data-extraction-policy.md`. Schema/DDIC (`GetTable`, `GetStructure`, `GetView`, `GetDataElement`, `GetDomain`) is always allowed.
6. **`acknowledge_risk` requires explicit user affirmative** (`yes` / `승인` / `authorize` / `approve` / `proceed` / `confirmed`). Ambiguous commands (`뽑아봐`, `try it`, `pull it`, `my mistake`) are NOT authorization. Per-call, per-table, per-session — never carries over. Full protocol: `common/data-extraction-policy.md` → "The `acknowledge_risk` Parameter — HARD RULE".
7. **Industry context matters.** For config analysis / business process design / Fit-Gap: load the project's `industry/<key>.md` (from `config.json` → `industry` or `sap.env` → `SAP_INDUSTRY`). If unset, ask the user.
8. **Country / localization context matters.** For tax, e-invoicing, banking, statutory reporting, date/number formats: load the project's `country/<iso>.md` (from `config.json` → `country` or `sap.env` → `SAP_COUNTRY`, ISO alpha-2 lowercase: `kr`, `us`, `de`, `eu-common`, …). Multi-country projects load every relevant file and flag cross-country touchpoints (intercompany, intra-EU VAT, transfer pricing). If unset, ask the user.

Enforcement: L1 agent instructions → L2 this file → L3 `PreToolUse` hook (`scripts/hooks/block-forbidden-tables.mjs`) → L4 MCP server upstream guard.

## Plugin Usage

### Skills (`/sc4sap:` prefix)
- `/sc4sap:setup` — Initial plugin setup + SPRO config generation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:create-program` — Full ABAP program pipeline (Phase 0–8) with execution-mode gate (auto/manual/hybrid) and parallel Phase 4/6; auto-invokes `trust-session` at Phase 1
- `/sc4sap:create-object` — Single ABAP object creation (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:program-to-spec` — Reverse-engineer a program into a spec artifact
- `/sc4sap:program-to-manual` — End-user manual for one program: one HTML file, scenario steps on drawn screens with numbered callouts, check points, field reference, messages & actions, glossary, revision history; one step per A4 landscape page in print. Output `.sc4sap/manuals/<PROGRAM>-v<n>-<lang>.html` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-code` — Static code review (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:compare-programs` — Business-angle side-by-side comparison of 2–5 ABAP programs sharing the same scenario but differing by module / country / persona (reader = consultant) → one editable, versioned HTML report (verdict matrix + *Differences only*, field differences, screens side by side, decision guide, English companion) `comparisons/<NAME>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:config-to-document` — One module's configuration documented from the live system: IMG tree, per IMG activity the real table values drawn on an SM30-style screen, customer-changed rows with their transports, configuration checks, SAP IMG documentation, consultant notes written by the module consultant agent and reviewed by `sap-critic` → one HTML file `config-docs/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-config-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base. MM first.
- `/sc4sap:interface-mapping-spec` — Interface mapping specification as one editable HTML page in the classic template layout (cover, revision history, header, Source → Target grid with R / MAPPING, optional synchronous response block, conversion rules, extraction condition, field guide). SAP side read from DDIC / FM signature or, for new interfaces, from a `TABLE-FIELD` list or the module consultant's proposal; counterpart fields, DB types, conversion rules and scenario defaults proposed; in-page checks; versioned with English companion → `interfaces/<IF_ID>/<IF_ID>-v<n>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base
- `/sc4sap:smartform-preview` — Expected print of one SmartForm without a print program: `GetSmartFormContent` (form XML, SmartStyle CSS, SE78 graphics) → windows drawn at their mm positions with templates, loops (sample rows) and graphics; `&fields&` filled with invented sample values sized to the DDIC types; report of cut-off cells / windows → `smartforms/<FORM>/<FORM>-preview.{jpg,html}` + `values.json` under the profile artifact base. Read-only.
- `/sc4sap:smartform-from-pdf` — SmartForm from a PDF (or screenshot) of a printed form: `read-pdf` (texts / rules / images in mm) → `plan-form` (rules → templates, texts in the formats of existing SmartStyles — no style is created) → fields, item loops and interface decided with the user (`shape-form`) → `write-form` (Form Builder XML) → `CreateSmartForm` on DEV → `RenderSmartForm` → `compare-layout` score against the source page → `smartforms/<FORM>/` under the profile artifact base. Writes (DEV only).
- `/sc4sap:project-dashboard` — SAP project dashboard for the PM / PMO: one editable HTML page per project (summary, KPIs, milestones with Q-gates, WBS with Gantt, team, history) from a project-type template, plus `projects/portfolio-<lang>.html` over every project; module vs development consultant tracked per WRICEF stage; actuals read from the connected system via `scripts/project/build-project-doc.mjs` (read-only) → `projects/<CODE>/` under the profile artifact base
- `/sc4sap:role-matrix` — Role & authorization workbook (business roles, PFCG roles, role × T-code F/C/D, user × role, authorization objects, SoD with conflict check, history): new design from the module consultant's proposal narrowed by ST03N, or `sync` from SAP (AGR_DEFINE / TEXTS / FLAGS / AGRS / TCODES / 1251 / 1252 / USERS — user IDs only, USR* never) via `scripts/role/build-role-doc.mjs`; paged sheets for large systems → `roles/<CODE>/` under the profile artifact base. Read-only on SAP.
- `/sc4sap:analyze-symptom` — Dump/error root-cause analysis (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` — Inventory a CBO package → save frequently-used Z objects to `.sc4sap/cbo/<MODULE>/<PACKAGE>/` for reuse by `create-program` / `program-to-spec` (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:cbo-relation-map` — One self-contained HTML relation map per package from the `graph.json` of `analyze-cbo-obj` (no SAP call): one or several packages; overview (hubs by business relations, usage, Louvain groups with names), Obsidian-style neighbourhood view (presets, filters by kind / type / basis / usage / package), impact up to the TCodes, shortest paths with alternatives, table CRUD tab, ±10-line source snippets, PNG / CSV export; includes folded into their owner; customer objects only (standard check tables as panel text). Missing graph → `collect.md` (whole package, or used TCodes only → `<PACKAGE>.used/`; eco = map-only collection) → `cbo/<MODULE>/<PACKAGE>/<PACKAGE>-relation-map-{ko,en}.html` or `cbo/<MODULE>/_relmap/` under the profile artifact base
- `/sc4sap:module-to-process` — One editable HTML process map per module (or process area), built only from the TCodes users actually run (productive ST03N via `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST`, or a saved / submitted usage list): used TCodes → programs → sources → reference graph → standard L1–L4 backbone (`configs/<M>/process-backbone.json`) → Opus hierarchy + PDD task sheets → optional module-consultant review → `assemble-model.mjs` → `build-process-doc.mjs` (BPH table, L3 scenario swimlanes, variant matrix, task sheets, appendix; edit mode + `--import`); optional BPH reconciliation (`bph-import.mjs`) and English companion (`companion.mjs`). Output `processes/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-process-v<ver>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — redirect to `module-to-process` for one release
- `/sc4sap:ask-consultant` — Direct user-facing Q&A with a module consultant agent (SD/MM/FI/CO/PP/PS/PM/QM/TR/HCM/WM/TM/BW/Ariba/BC). Auto-routes by keywords, answers against the configured SAP environment. Read-only (no writes, no row extraction).
- `/sc4sap:mcp-setup` — MCP ABAP ADT server configuration guide
- `/sc4sap:sap-option` — View and edit `.sc4sap/sap.env` (credentials, industry, blocklist profile, HUD limits)
- `/sc4sap:sap-doctor` — Diagnose plugin / MCP / SAP connection health
- `/sc4sap:trust-session` — INTERNAL-ONLY — session-wide MCP permission bootstrap; direct invocation is rejected

### Agents
- Core: `sap-analyst`, `sap-architect`, `sap-code-reviewer`, `sap-critic`, `sap-debugger`, `sap-doc-specialist`, `sap-executor`, `sap-planner`, `sap-qa-tester`, `sap-writer`
- Checker: `sap-checker` — Haiku, read-only fan-out worker (`scout` / `verify` / `detect`) that returns structured lines; the main thread dispatches N of them and one Opus agent consumes the result. Used by `/sc4sap:create-program` Phase 1A scout, Phase 4 verification, Phase 6 `detect-judge`; `/sc4sap:analyze-code` size scout, large-object detect-judge, evidence verify; `/sc4sap:compare-programs` facts extraction; `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` + `/sc4sap:package-to-process` stocking scouts.
- Discovery: `sap-stocker` — CBO inventory / where-used graph / reusable object cataloging (Sonnet, R/O SAP + R/W on `.sc4sap/cbo/`). Consumed by `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj`, `/sc4sap:create-program` (CBO reuse gate), and module consultants via their `<CBO_Stocking_Delegation>` block.
- Basis: `sap-bc-consultant`
- Module consultants: `sap-sd-`, `sap-mm-`, `sap-pp-`, `sap-pm-`, `sap-qm-`, `sap-wm-`, `sap-tm-`, `sap-tr-`, `sap-fi-`, `sap-co-`, `sap-hcm-`, `sap-bw-`, `sap-ps-`, `sap-ariba-consultant`

### SPRO Config Reference
`configs/{MODULE}/` contains `spro.md`, `tcodes.md`, `bapi.md`, `tables.md`, `enhancements.md`, `workflows.md` per module. Consultant agents consult these + `common/spro-lookup.md` before IMG answers.

### MCP Server (mcp-abap-adt)
All SAP interactions go through the MCP ABAP ADT server (150+ tools):
- CRUD: `CreateClass` / `UpdateClass` / `GetClass` / `DeleteClass` (and every DDIC/runtime object type)
- Analysis: `GetAbapAST`, `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis`, `GetWhereUsed`
- Runtime: `RunUnitTest`, `GetUnitTestResult`, `RuntimeAnalyzeDump`
- System: `GetTableContents`, `GetSqlQuery` (gated — see rule 5/6 above)
- Transport: `CreateTransport`, `GetTransport`, `ListTransports`

- `/sc4sap:module-to-process` — One editable HTML process map per module (or process area), built only from the TCodes users actually run (productive ST03N via `SAP_USAGE_RFCDEST`, or a saved / submitted usage list): used TCodes → programs → sources → reference graph → standard L1–L4 backbone (`configs/<M>/process-backbone.json`) → Opus hierarchy + PDD task sheets → optional module-consultant review → `assemble-model.mjs` → `build-process-doc.mjs` (BPH table, L3 scenario swimlanes, variant matrix, task sheets, appendix; edit mode + `--import`); optional BPH reconciliation (`bph-import.mjs`) and English companion (`companion.mjs`). Output `processes/<MODULE>/<MODULE>-process-v<ver>-<lang>.html` under the profile artifact base (auto-invokes `trust-session`)
- `/sc4sap:package-to-process` — redirect to `module-to-process` for one release
- `/sc4sap:ask-consultant` — Direct user-facing Q&A with a module consultant agent (SD/MM/FI/CO/PP/PS/PM/QM/TR/HCM/WM/TM/BW/Ariba/BC). Auto-routes by keywords, answers against the configured SAP environment. Read-only (no writes, no row extraction).
- `/sc4sap:mcp-setup` — MCP ABAP ADT server configuration guide
- `/sc4sap:sap-option` — View and edit `.sc4sap/sap.env` (credentials, industry, blocklist profile, HUD limits)
- `/sc4sap:sap-doctor` — Diagnose plugin / MCP / SAP connection health
- `/sc4sap:trust-session` — INTERNAL-ONLY — session-wide MCP permission bootstrap; direct invocation is rejected

### Agents
- Core: `sap-analyst`, `sap-architect`, `sap-code-reviewer`, `sap-critic`, `sap-debugger`, `sap-doc-specialist`, `sap-executor`, `sap-planner`, `sap-qa-tester`, `sap-writer`
- Checker: `sap-checker` — Haiku, read-only fan-out worker (`scout` / `verify` / `detect`) that returns structured lines; the main thread dispatches N of them and one Opus agent consumes the result. Used by `/sc4sap:create-program` Phase 1A scout, Phase 4 verification, Phase 6 `detect-judge`; `/sc4sap:analyze-code` size scout, large-object detect-judge, evidence verify; `/sc4sap:compare-programs` facts extraction; `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj` + `/sc4sap:package-to-process` stocking scouts.
- Discovery: `sap-stocker` — CBO inventory / where-used graph / reusable object cataloging (Sonnet, R/O SAP + R/W on `.sc4sap/cbo/`). Consumed by `/sc4sap:analyze-cbo-obj`, `/sc4sap:create-program` (CBO reuse gate), and module consultants via their `<CBO_Stocking_Delegation>` block.
- Basis: `sap-bc-consultant`
- Module consultants: `sap-sd-`, `sap-mm-`, `sap-pp-`, `sap-pm-`, `sap-qm-`, `sap-wm-`, `sap-tm-`, `sap-tr-`, `sap-fi-`, `sap-co-`, `sap-hcm-`, `sap-bw-`, `sap-ps-`, `sap-ariba-consultant`

### SPRO Config Reference
`configs/{MODULE}/` contains `spro.md`, `tcodes.md`, `bapi.md`, `tables.md`, `enhancements.md`, `workflows.md` per module. Consultant agents consult these + `common/spro-lookup.md` before IMG answers.

### MCP Server (mcp-abap-adt)
All SAP interactions go through the MCP ABAP ADT server (150+ tools):
- CRUD: `CreateClass` / `UpdateClass` / `GetClass` / `DeleteClass` (and every DDIC/runtime object type)
- Analysis: `GetAbapAST`, `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis`, `GetWhereUsed`
- Runtime: `RunUnitTest`, `GetUnitTestResult`, `RuntimeAnalyzeDump`
- System: `GetTableContents`, `GetSqlQuery` (gated — see rule 5/6 above)
- Transport: `CreateTransport`, `GetTransport`, `ListTransports`

</system-reminder>

# Evidence Receipt — Done Criteria decided by a script, not by an agent

Companion of [`verification-evidence.md`](verification-evidence.md) (Rule 2). There, the agent writes the Evidence block from the tool results it saw. A receipt takes that job away from the agent: the verdict of each check comes from the MCP responses themselves, recorded by a hook and judged by a script.

Scope today: `create-program` Phase 8. Same cost in `standard` and `eco` — no extra agent; at most one extra `GetInactiveObjects` call.

## How it works

| Part | File | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| Ledger — one line per SAP check or write call (time, tool, object names, parsed result, sha256 of the response) | `.sc4sap/evidence/ledger.jsonl` | PostToolUse hook `scripts/evidence/record.mjs` |
| Receipt — PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN per check, overall verdict | `.sc4sap/program/{PROG}/receipt.json` | `scripts/evidence/build-receipt.mjs` |
| Guard — denies Write / Edit / shell writes to both paths | — | PreToolUse hook `scripts/evidence/guard.mjs` |

Calls by sub-agents are recorded too. Reading the ledger or the receipt goes through the Read tool.

## Checks

| Check | PASS | FAIL | NOT RUN |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activation` | every object of the run written via MCP has a successful `ActivateObjects` after its last write | the last activation failed for an object, or an object changed after its last activation | no activation of the program recorded |
| `inactive` | a `GetInactiveObjects` after the last activation and the last write lists none of the run's objects | own objects still listed | no such call after the last activation / change |
| `unit_test` | the newest ABAP Unit result for the run's containers has > 0 methods and no critical / fatal alert, and no write came after it | a failed method, a failed setup, or code changed after the run | no run, no result, or 0 methods |

"Objects of the run" = names starting with `{PROG}` plus the names passed with `--also` (classes, function groups, tables whose names do not start with `{PROG}`).

Overall verdict: `FAIL` if any check failed; `INCOMPLETE` if any counted check is NOT RUN; else `PASS`. `unit_test` counts only with `--unit-test required` — pass it when spec.md § *9. Done Criteria* lists unit tests.

Syntax: `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis` parses the source text it is given locally. It is not the SAP syntax check, so it is not a receipt check. The SAP syntax check runs inside `ActivateObjects`, so the `activation` check covers it.

## Procedure (main thread)

1. Run `node "<PLUGIN_ROOT>/scripts/evidence/build-receipt.mjs" {PROG} [--also A,B] [--unit-test required]`. It writes the receipt and prints the Evidence lines.
2. Exit code `0` PASS → go on. `1` FAIL → do not report done; go back to the phase that owns the failing check (activation → Phase 4 final step / Phase 7, unit test → Phase 5). `2` INCOMPLETE → if `inactive` is NOT RUN, call `GetInactiveObjects` once and run step 1 again; any check still NOT RUN is reported as NOT RUN.
3. Hand `receipt.json` to the report writer. The writer copies each check's status and result into the Evidence block word for word and may add excerpts. It never upgrades a status. It adds the receipt line `Receipt: <verdict> · .sc4sap/program/{PROG}/receipt.json`.

## What a receipt does not prove

- Business logic, data, or authorization behaviour. Rule 3 of `verification-evidence.md` still applies to each line.
- Writes done outside MCP (SE38 by hand, another tool) are not in the ledger. The ledger only sees this project's MCP calls.
- The guard blocks the easy edit paths, not every path. A script written elsewhere could still change the files. The user's check in the TCode stays the final gate.

Kill switch: `DISABLE_SC4SAP=1` disables the hooks. The receipt then shows NOT RUN, never PASS.

# Verification Evidence — decisions, done criteria, limits of a check

Rules for how a skill reports finished work, so the user can stand behind it. Most agent output is well written and mostly right. That makes it easy to accept without a second look. These rules put three things in front of the user that a summary hides: what the agent decided on its own, what was actually run to prove the result, and what that proof does not cover.

Scope: a skill applies this file when its MD links here (today `create-program` Phase 8 and `analyze-symptom`). Rule 2's fixed-up-front Done Criteria apply to skills that build something (`create-program`); an analysis skill (`analyze-symptom`) has no pass target, so its Evidence lines say `supports` / `contradicts` / `not run` relative to the stated root cause instead of PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN. It changes the report only — no extra MCP calls, no extra agents, same cost in `standard` and `eco`.

## Rule 1 — Decisions & Assumptions section

Every final deliverable carries a section **Decisions & Assumptions** listing the choices the agent made that the user did not state explicitly. One line each:

`- <decision> — why: <reason> · to change: <what the user would do>`

What belongs here:

| Kind | Example |
|---|---|
| Default chosen | ALV layout save allowed for all users; date range defaults to current month |
| Out of scope | No authorization check on plant (not in the spec); no batch variant |
| Conflict resolved | Spec said "show all items", interview said "open items only" → open items only |
| Unverified assumption | Assumed `ZMMT0012-STATUS` values are `A`/`I` only (domain has no fixed values) |
| Scope narrowing | Read the failing include only, not the whole program; transports of the last 7 days only |

What does not belong: choices the user made in the interview (a default the agent proposed and the user only acknowledged with ok / yes does belong — the user did not choose it), choices fixed by a `common/` rule (naming, field typing), and restating the spec. If there is nothing to list, write the heading with "None — every choice came from the spec or the user." Never drop the section.

Order: most consequential first. Cap at 10 lines; past 10, group the rest by kind ("+ 6 text-element defaults").

## Rule 2 — Done criteria fixed up front, evidence shown first

A skill states what "verified" means **before** the work starts, as a short list of factual checks — a tool call and the result that counts as pass. Example for a program:

| Check | Pass |
|---|---|
| `ActivateObjects` on every created object | no error messages |
| `GetInactiveObjects` | none of this run's objects listed |
| `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis(<main program>)` — includes are not checked standalone | no errors |
| `RunUnitTest` (when Phase 5 ran) | all tests green, count > 0 |

Do not redefine "done" after the result is in. If a check could not run (tool missing, ECC limit, user skipped Phase 5), the result is **not run** — never pass.

In the report, the **Evidence** block comes before the summary. One line per check:

`- <tool> <target> → <result as returned, short excerpt> — PASS | FAIL | NOT RUN`

Quote the returned value (message text, count, object list); do not paraphrase it into "looks fine". The summary may only claim what an evidence line shows.

## Rule 3 — What the check does not prove

Each PASS line, or the Evidence block as a whole, carries the limits of that check:

`  ↳ does not prove: <property the check cannot see>`

Typical limits:

| Check | Does not prove |
|---|---|
| Activation / syntax check | business logic is right; runtime behavior with real data |
| `GetInactiveObjects` empty | objects are on the right transport |
| Unit tests green | cases the tests do not cover; tests written with the same mistake as the code pass too |
| Code review PASS | only the conventions reviewed; not the requirement itself |
| Dump explained by the source | that this is the only path to the dump; that the fix has no side effects |
| A tool's success message | that the target screen (SE80, Form Painter, SM30) shows it the same way |

End the report with one line that names the one thing a person should still check by hand before relying on the result (for example "Run the program once in DEV with a real plant and compare the totals with MB52").

## Placement in a report

```
## Evidence            ← Rule 2 (+ Rule 3 lines)
## Summary             ← claims backed by Evidence only
## Decisions & Assumptions   ← Rule 1
## Still check by hand ← Rule 3 closing line
```

A skill whose output format already has its own sections keeps them and inserts these where its MD says.

## Language

Localize the section headings to the report language. The verdict tokens (PASS / FAIL / NOT RUN, supports / contradicts / not run) stay in English.

- **activation:** 객체를 고친 뒤 다시 활성화하지 않았으면 FAIL이에요.

- **unit_test:** 테스트가 0건이면 NOT RUN이에요. 테스트 뒤에 코드를 고쳤으면 FAIL이에요.
- 다른 프로그램의 호출은 영수증에 섞이지 않아요.

- self-closing `<testMethod/>` 태그 때문에 테스트 수가 잘못 세졌어요. 수정했어요.
- 홈 폴더의 `~/.sc4sap`(전역 설정)를 프로젝트로 착각했어요. 그래서 테스트 데이터가 `~/.sc4sap/evidence`에 기록됐어요. 테스트가 남긴 데이터뿐이라 바로 지웠고 회귀 테스트도 추가했어요.

- **문법 검사 기준:** `GetAbapSemanticAnalysis`는 넘겨받은 소스를 로컬에서 분석해요. SAP 문법 검사가 아니에요. 그래서 문법 검사 증거는 `ActivateObjects` 결과로 삼았어요.

---
name: sc4sap plugin — 3-location sync when patching
description: When patching sc4sap plugin code, keep project source + marketplace + user cache in sync (user is plugin author, publishes from project folder)
type: reference
originSessionId: 624e4d17-84e6-4cca-a52f-34db7cd7ad7e
---
User authors the sc4sap plugin. When patching plugin code (bridge, scripts, hooks, skills), THREE locations must stay in sync:

1. **Project source (distribution source-of-truth)** — `C:/Users/pssps/Documents/Projects/sc4sap_project/sc4sap/`
   - This is what gets published to the marketplace.
   - All new fixes MUST land here first (for git/CHANGELOG).
2. **Marketplace copy (install-time source)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/sc4sap/`
   - What Claude Code ships into the cache when the plugin is enabled/updated.
3. **Cache (runtime)** — `C:/Users/pssps/.claude/plugins/cache/sc4sap/sc4sap/<version>/`
   - What actually runs. A fresh plugin install copies from marketplace → cache, overwriting ad-hoc patches here.

**Patching workflow**:
- Edit project source first.
- Mirror to marketplace (for install-time correctness).
